sections.h2: A $6.5 trillion financing gap sits inside the $22.7 trillion Net Zero bill

chart.title: Domestic sources cannot close the gap in India's Net Zero investment need
chart.sub: Cumulative investment by 2070 under NITI Aayog's Net Zero scenario, $ trillion.
chart.source: NITI Aayog, Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero, Vol. 9 (Financing Needs), February 2026.
chart.accent: Financing gap, domestic sources fall short
rows: Financing gap, domestic sources fall short

sections.means: NITI Aayog's own modelled estimate shows the Net Zero pathway needs outside finance on a large scale.
sections.todo: Secure cheaper external finance, as the CEO's five-step strategy proposes.

sections.h2: Non-fossil capacity is already past the 2015 target and near the 2035 goal

chart.title: Non-fossil capacity reached 52.57% before the 60% target for 2035
chart.source: Cabinet approval of India's NDC for 2031-2035, 25 March 2026; NITI Aayog.

sections.means: India has beaten its last capacity target early, which is the track record the new NDC relies on.
sections.todo: Keep the capacity build-out on pace, since coal still rises in absolute terms until 2047.

sections.h2: Emissions intensity cut of 36% by 2020 is the base for a 47% cut by 2035

chart.title: The new 2035 target asks for 11 points more intensity cut than was achieved by 2020
chart.sub: Reduction in GDP emissions intensity from a 2005 base, %.
chart.source: Cabinet approval of India's NDC for 2031-2035, 25 March 2026.

sections.means: The NDC raises the intensity ambition well above what India had already delivered.
sections.todo: Track intensity against the 47% goal each year, as the NDC's ahead-of-schedule record suggests.
